papers.title: Modular Ti-6Al-4V system for in vitro optimization of implant materials
papers.abstract: Introduction Titanium is a widely used biomaterial for implants. Research is focused on optimizing titanium by modifying its surface structure and porosity to prevent complications such as implant loosening or foreign body reactions. However, changes to implant materials necessitates preclinical testing, often involving animal testing, which gives rise to ethical concerns. This underscores the significant demand for test systems that can reduce time and costs. Although in vitro models can provide valuable initial insights into the biological evaluation of biomaterials and help reduce the need for animal experiments, dedicated test systems for biomaterial evaluation remain limited. Methods In our work, we developed modular 3D porous stacked models using Ti-6Al-4V sheets with different structural designs. These models are used to demonstrate the migration of primary human fibroblasts into the implant through fluorescence microscopy and investigate the effects of pore size. In addition, Ti alloy sheets with slots were polished and ground (1,200 grid SiC) to examine differences in cell adhesion and migration for different surface properties. Results The MTT results indicate similar cell growth on the different patterns and surface conditions, which suggests the use of more biomimetic structures in the future. Discussion Consequently, our model serves as a screening system for optimization of porosity and surface conditions of implant materials, which contributes to early-stage in vitro biocompatibility and cell migration studies.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文主要关注Ti-6Al-4V植入材料的体外生物相容性评估，而非其力学性能或疲劳行为，因此与L1方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: The paper focuses on in vitro biological evaluation (cell migration, biocompatibility) of Ti-6Al-4V implant materials, with no mechanical testing, fatigue analysis, or any mechanical/fatigue characterization.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发用于优化钛植入体材料和结构的测试系统以减少动物实验。
summary_zh.method: 使用不同孔隙和表面处理的Ti-6Al-4V片材构建模块化3D多孔模型。
summary_zh.result: 细胞生长在不同结构和表面上相似，表明可进一步使用仿生结构。
summary_zh.validation: 通过荧光显微镜、MTT实验等体外细胞实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a test system for optimizing implant materials and reducing animal testing by evaluating Ti-6Al-4V porous structures.
summary_en.method: Modular 3D porous stacked models were fabricated from Ti-6Al-4V sheets with varying pore sizes and surface finishes.
summary_en.result: MTT assays showed similar cell growth across different patterns and surface conditions, suggesting the potential for more biomimetic designs.
summary_en.validation: In vitro experiments using fluorescence microscopy and MTT assays assessed cell adhesion and migration.

papers.title: Precision measurement and sustainable assessment in milling of additively manufactured TiC–Ti64-ELI composites
papers.abstract: The quality of the machined surface and reduced carbon footprint are crucial factors for the operational effectiveness and lifetime of the manufactured components. Direct energy deposition (DED) can be employed to create large and complex metal parts, but low-dimensional accuracy usually requires finishing by a subtractive process. The present work deals with the sustainability assessment and machinability analysis in the machining of laser-melted titanium-based composites (TiC–Ti64-ELI) for the aviation sector. In this regard, the milling experiments were performed under distinct environmentally friendly cooling conditions. The results were analyzed in terms of environmental concerns, such as carbon emissions and specific cutting energy, as well as machining quality characteristics, including surface roughness and tool wear. The results indicate that cryogenic cooling with the carbon dioxide (Cryo-CO2) technique with laser-melted titanium composites can significantly lower carbon emissions while maintaining high-quality performance standards required in aviation applications. The desirability function was employed to obtain the best speed-feed combinations and environmental conditions for milling TiC–Ti64-ELI. The derived optimal conditions are Vc = 60 m/min, fr = 0.082 mm/rev, and Cryo-CO2 cooling. In addition, sustainable assessment was employed to study the effectiveness of environmental conditions.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及TiC–Ti64-ELI复合材料的铣削后处理，但材料并非纯Ti-6Al-4V，且未评估疲劳/力学性能。
llm.why_not_core: Paper studies milling of TiC-Ti64-ELI composite, not pure Ti-6Al-4V, and focuses on machinability and sustainability rather than the effect on fatigue or mechanical performance.

summary_zh.motivation: 提高增材制造钛基复合材料机加工表面质量并降低碳排放。
summary_zh.method: 在不同冷却条件下进行TiC–Ti64-ELI铣削实验，分析表面粗糙度、刀具磨损和碳排放。
summary_zh.result: 二氧化碳低温冷却在降低碳排放的同时保持了高质量表面。
summary_zh.validation: 通过铣削实验和期望函数优化工艺参数验证。

summary_en.motivation: To improve machined surface quality and reduce carbon footprint in subtractive finishing of additively manufactured titanium matrix composites.
summary_en.method: Milling experiments on DED-fabricated TiC–Ti64-ELI were conducted under cryogenic, MQL, and dry conditions, evaluating surface roughness, tool wear, specific cutting energy, and carbon emissions.
summary_en.result: Cryogenic CO₂ cooling achieved the best overall performance, significantly lowering carbon emissions while maintaining high surface quality.
summary_en.validation: Experimental machining trials and desirability function optimization validated the process parameters.
